confirmed_blocking.evidence: Static, deterministic schedule (not a timing race): relay A reads since, snapshots; job c is admitted; relay B dispatch_pending (claimed_at>=since) and enqueue(c) into the index; A's scheduler.rebuild wipes c; A's reopen_dispatch clears c's claimed_at/claimed_by (row still unacked); B's acknowledge_dispatch now lands (its only predicates are kind + acknowledged_at is null, 0012 l.293-296) -> returns 1, row 'delivered'; A's pump reads nothing for c. c sits preparing, not in any index, until its preparation deadline; nothing re-dispatches it (no periodic rebuild; integration request 7 rebuilds only at scheduler start). B's window (enqueue RTT -> ack) and A's window (reopen RTT -> dispatch_pending) are of the same order, so a rebuild racing a pump strands with real probability. The shipped racing drill (test_outbox__a_rebuild_racing_another_relays_pump_strands_no_job) puts B's whole pump, ack included, inside the snapshot hook, so it cannot see this ordering. Reviewer drill test_r2_ack_after_reopen_strands_the_job (ack in a reopen hook, all three adapters) and test_r2b (same schedule with the fix below) were scripted in the scratch copy but NOT executed: the session was cut off before the serial chain reached them (see fabrication_check).
